title: Constraint Graph-based PCB Legalization Considering Dense, Heterogeneous, Irregular-Shaped, and Any-oriented Components
problem: Modern PCB designs with dense, heterogeneous, irregular-shaped, and any-oriented components pose challenges for automatic placement legalization, especially double-sided designs. Existing methods rely on naive bounding box approximations and cannot handle complex constraints effectively.
method: First constraint graph-based legalization approach for PCBs. Uses slicing technique to model components accurately via rectangles instead of bounding box approximation. Employs Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to expand solution space for heterogeneous, irregular-shaped, any-oriented components in high-density designs.

title: 8.8 Fine-Grained Spatial and Temporal Thermal Profiling of a 16nm CMOS Buck Converter and SoC Load-Current Emulator Using Low-Voltage Micron-Scale Thermal Sensors
problem: Localized thermal hotspots in high-power-density SoCs and 3D systems with integrated voltage regulators create fine-grained temperature gradients (>10°C across 100μm scales), limiting performance and reliability of AI/ML accelerators and special-purpose compute units.
method: The work develops low-voltage micron-scale thermal sensors for fine-grained spatial and temporal thermal profiling. A 16nm CMOS buck converter and SoC load-current emulator demonstrate the sensor architecture's ability to capture localized thermal hotspot profiles across heterogeneous workloads.

title: 36.5 A Low-Latency 200Gb/s PAM-4 Heterogeneous Transceiver in 0.13µm SiGe BiCMOS and 28nm CMOS for Retimed Pluggable Optics
problem: AI infrastructure demands 200G/lane serial links for data-center interconnects, but linear-drive pluggable optics (LPO) face severe challenges at 200G: very-short-reach (VSR) channel insertion loss increases by 14dB at 2x data rate (to -14dB overall), and retimed LPO solutions (with DSP) introduce unacceptable latency (incompatible with low-latency AI inference requirements). Traditional 200G retimed schemes mitigate 30dB insertion loss via DSP compensation, but this adds significant pipeline delay.
method: A heterogeneous transceiver architecture combining SiGe BiCMOS analog front-end (0.13µm) and 28nm CMOS digital logic. The key innovation is a non-ADC-based receiver eliminating the DSP delay bottleneck. Analog equalization on the SiGe side handles severe VSR channel insertion loss without requiring DSP; 28nm CMOS integrates clock/data recovery and link-layer functions. This heterogeneous approach achieves comparable energy efficiency to retimed solutions while maintaining near-zero additional latency.

title: Hardware Implementation of Blind Decoding of Downlink Control Information for 5G
problem: 5G user equipment (UE) must blindly decode Downlink Control Information (DCI) from multiple candidate locations within 0.25 ms stringent time limit. Exhaustive search across candidates is computationally intensive and imposes significant latency, risking missed decoding deadlines.
method: Flexible hardware implementation for blind DCI decoding optimizing resource utilization to complete within time budget. Implemented on Xilinx Zynq Ultrascale+ RFSoC ZCU111 board with integration into existing 5G testbed UE receive chain. Tested and validated with in-house 5G testbed.

title: Implementing OpenMP Offload Support in the AMD Next Generation Fortran Compiler
problem: Fortran remains dominant in HPC but classic Flang compiler limiting; modern supercomputers use GPUs (heterogeneous), requiring OpenMP offload support for GPU targeting; missing compiler support hinders Fortran adoption on GPU-accelerated systems.
method: AMD Next Generation Fortran Compiler (AMD Flang) implements OpenMP target directives and map clauses. Describes compilation pipeline, code generation for target offload, and intermediate representation transformations (e.g., DO CONCURRENT via OpenMP IR).

title: IRIS: A 8.55mJ/frame Spatial Computing SoC for Interactable Rendering and Surface-Aware Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: Interactive Spatial Computing (ISC) for mixed-reality (MR) requires real-time surface-aware modeling (SAM) and interactive photorealistic rendering (IPR) with tight latency budgets (15ms) and high computational demands. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables superior quality but faces three challenges: (1) massive external memory access (EMA) for unordered >50MB parameters exceeds edge GPU L2 cache (4MB), (2) IPR requires three sequential stages (deform/reflect/render) causing 2.33x overhead vs. non-interactive rendering, (3) backpropagation for SAM consumes 55.8% of compute due to FP16 precision and limited reusability.
method: IRIS SoC implements Single-Embedding-Multi-MLP (SEMM)-based 3DGS compression reducing parameter size while preserving quality. The architecture features specialized datapath for SAM and IPR stages, optimized memory hierarchy to minimize EMA, and hardware reuse for backpropagation to reduce compute redundancy. Spatial computing-aware scheduling and memory orchestration keep all processing within tight 15ms latency budget.

title: coMtainer: Compilation-assisted HPC Container Images with Enhanced Adaptability
problem: Containers simplify HPC deployment but fail to deliver optimal performance due to separated build/execution workflows, missing system-specific optimizations.
method: coMtainer embeds build-time information into containers, enabling remote HPC systems to specialize images with native toolchains and apply LTO/PGO optimizations.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper Bine Trees: Enhancing Collective Operations by Optimizing Communication Locality
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility assessment of Bine Trees collective communication optimization technique
method: Systematic artifact evaluation following SC25 Reproducibility Initiative guidelines for collective communication optimization work

title: 6.5 A 25.2Mpixel 120frames/s Full-Frame Global-Shutter CMOS Image Sensor with Pixel-Parallel ADC
problem: Conventional rolling-shutter sensors have image distortion, flicker effects, and flash bands; previous global-shutter approaches (charge-domain, voltage-domain) fail to meet consumer ILC camera requirements for dynamic range and random noise; scaling pixel-parallel ADCs to tens of megapixels while maintaining image quality and low power consumption is challenging.
method: 25.2Mpixel 120fps full-frame sensor using pixel-parallel ADC in stacked structure, achieving global shutter with high dynamic range and low random noise by distributing ADC processing at pixel level.

title: Advancing Neural Network Performance with Probabilistic Computing for ReLU Function
problem: Neural networks require efficient ReLU activation functions on hardware. Probabilistic computing (p-bits) offers invertible bidirectional operations but ReLU implementation details for p-circuits are underexplored.
method: Framework for designing p-circuits using p-bits (stochastic bit representations). ReLU design using Hamiltonian method with two variants: (1) AND gate-based, (2) non-imply logic gate-based. Also designs 2x1 multiplexer and AB non-imply logic gate.

title: pulse: Accelerating Distributed Pointer-Traversals on Disaggregated Memory
problem: CPU-side caches in disaggregated memory architectures cannot amortize network latency for pointer-chasing workloads over linked data structures, because each traversal step depends on the preceding one, making prefetching and caching ineffective.
method: pulse is a distributed pointer-traversal framework that executes pointer-chasing computations close to disaggregated memory rather than at CPU nodes. Traversal kernels are offloaded to processing elements co-located with memory, supporting various linked data structures with a programmable traversal interface. The framework supports distributed execution across multiple memory nodes for rack-scale workloads, preserving expressiveness while improving latency, throughput, and energy efficiency relative to cache-based access.

title: Aqua: Network-Accelerated Memory Offloading for LLMs in Scale-Up GPU Domains
problem: LLM inference under bursty request patterns exhausts GPU memory, causing serving engines to use admission control that renders them unresponsive; preemptive time-sliced scheduling requires KV-cache paging that incurs high overhead and reduces throughput.
method: Aqua is a GPU memory management framework that uses the high-bandwidth scale-up network (NVLink/NVSwitch fabric within a server) as a fast memory offloading path for paging LLM inference state (KV caches). When a prompt is preempted, Aqua pages its KV cache over the scale-up network to remote GPU memory on other nodes rather than to slow host DRAM or NVMe, dramatically reducing paging latency. A scheduling layer enables preemptive time-sliced prompt execution on top of this low-overhead paging mechanism.

title: HIVE: A High-Priority Victim Cache for Accelerating GPU Memory Accesses
problem: GPU memory hierarchies suffer from high latency when victim caches are accessed as secondary L1D miss handlers, particularly for memory-intensive workloads.
method: HIVE redesigns the victim cache to handle memory requests before L1D access. High-priority victim cache provides direct low-latency memory request handling, bypassing the L1D cache for certain access patterns. Architectural modification prioritizes victim cache lookups for the most latency-critical requests.

title: ACIM-QMM: Efficient Analog Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for QC-MDPC McEliece Cryptosystem
problem: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementations like QC-MDPC McEliece suffer from high latency and large hardware overhead in digital computing paradigm.
method: ACIM-QMM leverages analog circuits and computing-in-memory to perform matrix operations required for QMM key generation and encryption, breaking the digital computing bottleneck while maintaining low relative error.

title: 23.8 An 88.36TOPS/W Bit-Level-Weight-Compressed Large-Language-Model Accelerator with Cluster-Aligned INT-FP-GEMM and Bi-Dimensional Workflow Reformulation
problem: Large language model inference deployment faces three orthogonal challenges: (1) autoregressive generation requires 1000x more external memory accesses (EMA) per token vs. non-autoregressive transformers due to streaming weight reads and KV-cache updates; (2) mixed-precision (INT-FP) GEMM with quantized weights and FP activations typically requires dequantization overhead (4.6x power vs. native INT-FP), reducing quantization benefits; (3) special function units (softmax, trigonometric) create compute-memory coupling where processors wait 1/3 of time for SFU results.
method: Dedicated LLM accelerator employing three innovations: (1) bit-level weight compression with efficient INT-FP mixed-precision GEMM avoiding dequantization overhead while preserving quantization benefits; (2) cluster-aligned processing enabling efficient data movement and tiling across compressed weight formats; (3) bi-dimensional workflow reformulation decoupling GEMM and SFU operations, allowing PEs to continue while SFU processes non-linear functions asynchronously, eliminating PE stalls. Architecture optimizes for LLM memory-access patterns and compute-intensive non-linear operations.

title: Chimera: Communication Fusion for Hybrid Parallelism in Large Language Models
problem: Hybrid parallelism strategies (tensor, pipeline, sequence, data parallelism combined) for LLM training and inference on multi-NPU systems generate a large volume of diverse collective communications whose blocking nature severely throttles compute utilization. Redundant communication operators introduced by combining multiple parallelism dimensions compound this bottleneck.
method: Chimera performs a systematic analysis of communication processes for each parallelism dimension (tensor, pipeline, data, sequence), identifies redundant collective operations that arise when multiple parallelism strategies are combined, and eliminates them by fusing adjacent communication operators during parallelism transformation. It reorders operations and generates a single redundancy-free communication operator that achieves the semantics of the original multi-collective sequence. The resulting fused operator is injected into the LLM computation graph as a replacement for the original blocking collectives.
